macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise as Dow gains 1.1%
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.1%, the S&P 500 gained 0.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.1% on Thursday. Treasury yields fell, with the 10-year yield declining to 5.09% from 5.19%.

items.title: Fed chair keeps rate decisions open
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said he would not prejudge upcoming policy meetings while emphasizing the Fed’s commitment to price stability. Markets continued to price a high probability of another rate increase in December, amid concerns about persistent inflation.

items.title: U.S. producer inflation accelerates
items.summary: The producer price index rose 6.3% year over year in September, up from 5.6% in August and marking its largest annual increase since December 2022. The stronger inflation reading reinforced expectations that the Fed may keep rates higher for longer.

items.title: European shares edge higher
items.summary: Spain’s IBEX 35 rose 0.44% in early trading, while the FTSE Eurofirst 300 gained 0.27%. Investors awaited final September eurozone inflation data and U.S. industrial production figures.

items.title: Asian markets rebound after Wall Street gains
items.summary: Asian shares mostly recovered after Thursday’s gains in U.S. equities, although Indonesia’s market fell sharply after MSCI warned it could downgrade the country from emerging-market status.

items.title: Taiwan Semiconductor earnings support chip stocks
items.summary: U.S. stock futures pointed to a higher open as investors responded to a stronger-than-expected Taiwan Semiconductor earnings report and signs that semiconductor-sector selling pressure was easing.

items.title: Regional bank earnings take focus
items.summary: Investors are set to assess results from Travelers, Truist Financial, M&T Bank and Citizens Financial Group, with the reports expected to provide fresh signals on credit quality, net interest margins and commercial real-estate exposure.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $82,000 as major cryptocurrencies recover
items.summary: Bitcoin rose 1.9% to about $82,130, while Ether gained 3.6% to $2,443. XRP, Solana, and Cardano also advanced, though several major tokens remained lower for the week.[1]

items.title: Crypto liquidations near $1 billion as Bitcoin briefly falls below $80,000
items.summary: The global crypto market capitalization increased about 1% to $2.86 trillion after Bitcoin briefly dropped below $80,000. Approximately $932 million in leveraged positions were liquidated over 24 hours, predominantly long positions.[8]

items.title: EU regulators classify USDC as first significant e-money token under MiCA
items.summary: The European Banking Authority designated Circle’s USDC as the EU’s first significant e-money token. Direct EBA supervision of key parts of USDC’s operations is scheduled to begin November 12.[3]

items.title: White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt exits as Clarity Act stalls
items.summary: Patrick Witt has left his role as White House chief crypto adviser amid stalled digital-asset legislation, including the Clarity Act.[3]

items.title: Russia plans restrictions on peer-to-peer crypto trading
items.summary: The Russian central bank reportedly plans to prohibit direct person-to-person cryptocurrency transactions from July 2027, requiring individuals to use authorized intermediaries and restricting transfers from digital accounts to self-custody wallets.[2]

items.title: Ramp raises $1.85 billion at $60 billion valuation
items.summary: Crypto infrastructure company Ramp reportedly completed a funding round of $1.85 billion, with Dragoneer Investment Group, Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital, and Avenir Growth leading the round.[2]

items.title: Uniform Labs raises $8 million for Multiliquid
items.summary: Uniform Labs, the developer of Multiliquid, raised $8 million across pre-seed and seed financing rounds.[3]

items.title: Ledger announces Android-based Ledger Atom device
items.summary: Ledger announced Ledger Atom, an Android-based device designed to support everyday applications alongside a dedicated crypto-security mode and AI assistant; release is planned for mid-2027.[8]

items.title: Solana establishes Shanghai office despite China’s crypto restrictions
items.summary: The Solana Foundation has established a commercial presence in Shanghai and launched China-focused events while Chinese restrictions on cryptocurrency activity remain in effect.[10]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: New York bill would establish ownership of digital games
items.summary: Representative Ritchie Torres announced plans for legislation that would give consumers ownership rights over digitally purchased games rather than revocable licenses. The proposal follows increasing industry reliance on digital distribution and game shutdowns.

items.title: New game releases include Valor Mortis and Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse
items.summary: Recent releases across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC include Valor Mortis and Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, alongside other fall launches such as Gears of War: E-Day and Forever Ago.

items.title: Bryson Tiller announces Brutal Industry game for 2027
items.summary: Musician Bryson Tiller revealed Brutal Industry, a beat-’em-up inspired by the music business. The game is being developed through Trapsoul Games and is planned first for Arcade1Up cabinets, with broader platforms considered later.

items.title: Rockstar releases Grand Theft Auto VI launch trailer
items.summary: Rockstar Games reportedly released a launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI, with the game scheduled for November 19, 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. A PC version is expected later.

items.title: Capcom announces Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance expansion
items.summary: Capcom presented the first trailer for Ascendance, an expansion for Monster Hunter Wilds, during State of Play. The downloadable content is planned for 2027 on PC, Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5.

items.title: Until Dawn 2 set for January 2027 release
items.summary: Sony showed a new trailer for Until Dawn 2 and announced a January 28, 2027 release date. PlayStation Store preorders are reportedly open.

items.title: Epic Games Store begins testing redesigned launcher
items.summary: Epic Games introduced a substantially redesigned Epic Games Store launcher, with a preview available for Windows, macOS and, for the first time, Linux.
